name: DAAD Hilde Domin Programme (Master's for At-Risk Students)
requiredDocuments: Online nomination form completed by the nominating German institution/organisation (candidate cannot self-apply)
Questionnaire on the nominee's risk situation ('Risk description form') submitted as part of the nomination
Proof or credible demonstration of a threat to personal well-being or safety (e.g. physical violence, arrest, denial of civil/educational rights) provided to the nominating institution
Educational certificates enabling entrance to a German higher education institution (recognised per the anabin database)
Language certificate showing German or English at B2 level as required by the intended degree programme
Valid passport (still valid for at least one year on the DAAD application deadline; accompanying spouse/minor children must also hold valid passports)
Application via the DAAD online application portal after being invited following nomination (documents submitted in German or English)
For visual/performing arts, design, visual communication, music, film, architecture: a letter from an accredited higher-education institution confirming academic ability and willingness to enrol

timeline.opens: Nominations can be submitted online at any time; DAAD candidate application periods: 17 March - 15 April 2026 (summer semester 2027) and 17 September - 15 October 2026 (winter semester 2027/28)
timeline.deadline: Nominations by 15 March 2026 for summer semester 2027 start; nominations by 15 September 2026 for winter semester 2027/28 start
timeline.notes: Dates are the two cycles published on the official DAAD page as of 2026-06. The summer-semester-2027 nomination/application windows have already closed; the winter-semester-2027/28 windows (nominations by 15 Sep 2026, DAAD application 17 Sep - 15 Oct 2026) are the next open ones. Candidates do not apply directly - they are nominated, then invited by DAAD to apply within the application window. Nominating institutions run their own internal deadlines (e.g. TUM requires a nomination request 17-30 Aug 2026 for the winter 2027/28 round).

benefits: Monthly scholarship payment of currently 992 EUR for master's students (1,400 EUR for doctoral candidates)
Health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance based on country of origin / present residence
If applicable, a preparatory German language course (2, 4 or 6 months) according to required language skills
Funding for up to 24 months for a master's degree
Qualification through participation in interdisciplinary trainings

acceptanceRate.estimateNote: No acceptance/selection rate is published by DAAD. The DAAD page states 'The DAAD can only award a limited number of scholarships' and TUM's official page notes 'Demand usually greatly exceeds the number of scholarships available' - qualitative only, not a numeric rate.

mustKnow: You CANNOT self-apply: candidates must be nominated by the management of a German legal entity active in science/research/teaching and/or human-rights protection, peace, democracy or rule of law. Only after an initial DAAD plausibility check are suitable candidates invited to apply via the DAAD portal.

This is a protection programme for people at risk: you must prove or credibly demonstrate a personal threat (e.g. physical violence, arrest, denial of civil/educational rights) due to ethnic, sexual, gender or religious identity and/or political or civic engagement. Both risk status AND academic prospects are assessed.
Worldwide eligibility EXCEPT nationals of EU/EEA/EFTA countries, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino and the United Kingdom - Bangladesh is NOT excluded, so Bangladeshis are eligible.
You may NOT already be residing in Germany or the European Union at the time of nomination.
German or English at B2 level (matching the intended programme's language) is required by the nomination deadline.
Human medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, pharmacy and law are excluded disciplines; a second master's or doctoral degree is not funded.

TUITION IS NOT GUARANTEED: the scholarship covers a living stipend and insurance, not university tuition. At fee-charging universities (e.g. TUM, where non-EEA master's tuition is generally EUR 3,000 or EUR 6,000) DAAD does NOT pay the fees - apply for a waiver or choose a tuition-free university. Most German public universities charge no tuition.
Two-step process: a DAAD scholarship confirmation does NOT secure a study place - you must separately apply for and be admitted to a degree programme by the host university within its own deadlines.
Passport must be valid for at least one year on the DAAD application deadline (also for any accompanying spouse/minor children).
Multiple nominations give no advantage; one nomination per candidate suffices. Nominations via email/post/fax are not accepted.

universities: Any recognised higher education institution in Germany (degree programme of personal choice; e.g. Technical University of Munich)

duration: Up to 24 months for a master's degree
eligibleNationalities: Open to students/doctoral candidates worldwide who are at risk in their country of origin, EXCEPT nationals of EU/EEA/EFTA countries, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino and the United Kingdom. Bangladeshi nationals are eligible.
languageRequirements: German or English at B2 level (corresponding to the language of the intended programme) by the nomination deadline; the required language certificate for the specific degree programme must be provided.
applicationFee: Free (no application fee; application is via the DAAD portal after nomination)
bondObligation: None stated. The programme's long-term goal is for beneficiaries to contribute to development in their country of origin, in Germany or in third countries after completing studies, but no binding return/service obligation is imposed.
